title: Statement of financial position
author: DkfTkX7xNnbzLCF2p
chapter_outcomes: Have an understand of the different types of business entity; sole trader, partnership, limited company
Evaluate the  advantages and disadvantages of these types of business entity

Assess the sources of finance and methods of funding for these types of business entity including loans (secured and unsecured), bank overdrafts, payment by instalments, rental/leasing as an alternative to purchase, trade credit, and sources of finance for limited companies
Evaluate the difference between the treatment of capital and revenue income and capital and revenue expenditure
Assess the effect on profit/loss and asset value of the incorrect treatment of capital and revenue expenditure
Evaluate the factors that cause the value of non-current assets to depreciate
Understand the purpose of accounting for depreciation of non-current assets and the associated application of relevant accounting concepts
Know how to calculate depreciation using the reducing balance and straight-line methods
Understand the most appropriate method of calculating depreciation
Know how to measure the value of non-current assets by the cost model or the revaluation model
Know how to prepare ledger accounts and journal entries for non-current assets (acquisition and revaluation), and depreciation and disposal (including entries for part exchange)
Know how to calculate profit or loss on disposal of a non-current asset
Understand how to record the effect of a charge for depreciation in the statement of profit or loss and statement of financial position
Understand the need to reconcile and verify ledger accounts using documentation from internal and external sources
Evaluate the benefits and limitations of reconciliation and verification procedures
Identify errors which affect the trial balance
Identify errors which do not affect the trial balance; omission, commission, principle, original entry, reversal, and compensating
Understand how to prepare ledger accounts and journal entries to correct errors using a suspense account
Assess the effect on the financial statements of the correction of errors
Evaluate the benefits and limitations of a trial balance
Understand the updating of cash books
Know how to prepare bank reconciliation statements
Evaluate how to prepare bank reconciliation statements
Understand entries in control accounts
Understand sales ledger control accounts and purchases ledger control accounts
Understand reconciliation statements between control account balances and ledger balances
Assess the effects on financial statements of the correction of errors
Evaluate the benefits and limitations of control accounts

Understand how to calculate and record the adjustments needed and the effect on financial statements in respect of accruals and prepayments of income and expenses, irrecoverable debts, irrecoverable debts recovered and allowance for irrecoverable debts, depreciation, inventory valuation, and correction of errors
Know how to prepare a statement of profit or loss and statement of financial position for a sole trader from full or incomplete accounting records
Know how to prepare a statement of profit or loss, appropriation account and statement of financial position for a partnership from full or incomplete accounting records.
Understand why partners may maintain separate capital accounts and current accounts
Know how to prepare partners’ capital and current accounts
Understand the contents of a partnership agreement
Evaluate the advantages and disadvantages to partners of maintaining a partnership agreement
Understand the provisions of the Partnership Act 1890 in respect of partners’ salaries, division of profit or loss, interest on partners’ loans, interest on capital and interest on drawings
Understand the features and accounting treatment of ordinary shares, bonus issues, rights issues, debentures, dividends and reserves
Evaluate the advantages and disadvantages to the company and to the shareholders of a company making a bonus issue of shares and a rights issue of shares
Evaluate the advantages and disadvantages to the company and to the shareholders of a company issuing shares and issuing debentures
Assess the distinction between capital reserves (share premium and revaluation reserve) and revenue reserves (retained earnings and general reserve)
Know how to prepare ledger accounts to record an issue of ordinary shares at par or at a premium, a rights issue of shares at par or at a premium, and a bonus issue of shares
Know how to prepare a statement of profit or loss, statement of financial position and statement of changes in equity for a limited company.
Identify sources of finance for specified purposes
Understand the differing requirements for information of stakeholders including owners, managers, employees, investors, lenders, suppliers, customers, government, and public and environmental bodies
Know how to communicate and analyse the information required by these different stakeholders

Know how to calculate key accounting ratios to measure profitability, liquidity and efficiency: profitability ratios; gross profit margin, mark-up, profit margin, return on capital employed, expenses to revenue ratio (operating expenses to revenue ratio), liquidity ratios: current ratio, acid test ratio, and efficiency ratios: non-current asset turnover, trade receivables turnover (days), trade payables turnover (days), inventory turnover (days), rate of inventory turnover (times)
Know how to evaluate the profitability, liquidity and efficiency of an organisation by interpreting ratios
Evaluate possible measures to improve the profitability, liquidity and efficiency of an organisation
Evaluate the limitations of accounting information
